interpretation_rules: An assertion is a source-specific statement. An event is a provisional or qualified grouping of assertions about a physical or scheduled subject; they are not interchangeable.
Keep publication/report time, physical event valid time, sensor observation time and ledger-recorded time separate. Never copy one into another.
A relation is directional: from_assertion_id is the newer or dependent assertion; to_assertion_id is the earlier or referenced assertion.
Only merge assertions into one event with explicit identifiers or documented adjudication. Text similarity or suburb overlap alone is insufficient.
A schedule is an operating rule, not proof that each scheduled occurrence happened. Do not manufacture occurrence rows.
A status snapshot is not an incident, a sensor measurement or a time series. Percentages with undefined denominator/method are not comparable by default.
A publisher notice establishes that the publisher made the statement; it does not establish customer-level supply, affected-household counts, outage duration or independent restoration.
Missing event time, geometry, raw bytes, digest, licence, method or customer observations remain null/unknown; do not impute them.
Corrections and later notices append new assertions and relations. Never overwrite the earlier assertion or collapse conflicting accounts into last-write-wins state.
No event graph record authorizes utility control, service allocation, relocation, enforcement or any other consequential action.
claim_ceiling: A source-linked, manually reviewed, provisional grouping of selected Johannesburg Water notice assertions from the metadata-only source register. It is not a complete incident register, telemetry stream, verified geographic footprint, customer-service measurement, hydraulic calibration dataset or operational digital twin.
